clue.text: Part of horse's back becomes dry and shrivelled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades
second meaning: the verb for drying up and wrinkling, third person

explanation.surface: A horse's back is wasting away, drying up and wrinkling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of an ageing horse; it is two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the high point of a horse's shoulders, while the verb form describes plants or skin drying and shrinking.

clue.text: Women kick and hit

parts.note: to hack is to kick, as at the shins in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A self-defence class where women learn to kick and strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To whack is to strike forcefully, a near synonym of the verb meaning to deliver a blow.

clue.text: Have nothing good to say about cease-fire coming without notice

definitions.text: Have nothing good to say about

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A grumble about a truce declared with no warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without notice' looks like an idiom for suddenly, but without is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander or speak ill of someone, damaging their reputation.

clue.text: Cupid can help make lover ostentatious

indicators.note: the neighbouring words each contribute part, so together they make the answer

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The god of love may turn a suitor into a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of erotic love, the counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Pours elixir out with thud — a corrosive mixture

definitions.note: adjective used as a noun: a corrosive substance

indicators.note: poured out suggests spilled and scattered, so these letters are disordered
a mixture is a jumble, signalling the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A potion poured out with a bang turns out to be dangerous stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur trioxide is a highly reactive chemical that forms sulphuric acid with water and burns tissue.

clue.text: A set of new books, one which in Paris would be seen as old

parts.note: the New Testament is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A bookseller's set of new volumes, which a Parisian might regard as already dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of new books' is not about publishing: NT is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique item is one from an earlier era, so the adjective works as a synonym for aged or ancient.

clue.text: Ancient eras had a different statement of Christian belief

indicators.note: made different means changed, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Earlier ages held another version of the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athanasian Creed is a profession of faith on the Trinity, used in Western churches since the sixth century.

clue.text: Titles of commercial products could make admen stare

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Brand names so striking that advertising executives gape at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade names are the proprietary labels under which goods are sold, so brand titles for merchandise.

clue.text: Asked about what might be required when leader's gone

indicators.note: what a word might be suggests another possible arrangement of it
the leader of a word is its first letter, and here it has departed

explanation.surface: Someone enquiring what will be needed once the boss has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of the given word, then rearrange the seven that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To query something is to ask a question about it, so the past tense means enquired.

clue.text: Christian message on part of church that's seen when looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards means taking the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: The gospel message is visible when you gaze up at a church's ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: On and leg are the same side of a cricket pitch, the batsman's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, the good news preached by Christianity.

clue.text: Shiite leader always getting a number of people killed — my!

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for ever or always
the death toll is the count of fatalities

explanation.surface: A grim report on a cleric whose rule keeps costing lives, with a shocked exclamation at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: AY meaning always is old and poetic, as in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior religious authority among Shia Muslims, notably in Iran.

clue.text: This palm needs cold in the region

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters sit inside the second word

explanation.surface: A gardening note: this palm needs a chilly climate to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is botanically wrong, which is part of the disguise; ARE then C then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a genus of tropical palm trees, the source of the betel nut.

clue.text: King, one to act crazy!

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a nut is a madman, someone who behaves crazily

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a monarch who behaved madly.
explanation.walkthrough: Knut, or Canute, was the Danish-English king said to have ordered the tide to retreat, which the whole clue presents as crazy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of the eleventh-century monarch commanding the sea to halt makes him the ruler who acted madly.

clue.text: Very big object that's kept below

indicators.note: the object holds something within it, as a box keeps what is stored

explanation.surface: A huge item stored down in the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept below' reads as one phrase about storage, but below is the word placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundering is an informal intensifier meaning enormous or tremendous, as in a thundering great lie.

clue.text: We shall get a bit of heat and even bits of rain, according to him

definitions.text: We shall get a bit of heat and even bits of rain, according to him

parts.note: a therm is a unit of heat

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, are kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of rain

explanation.surface: A forecast of some warmth and a few showers, as given on the evening news.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the forecaster's message, with 'according to him' pointing to who says it.
explanation.definitionFit: A weatherman is a meteorologist who presents forecasts, predicting sunshine and showers on television.

clue.text: There's a superficial pretence with the archdeacon always

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A dig at a churchman whose show of piety is permanently fake.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon carries the title 'the Venerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin attractive surface layer, so figuratively an outward show hiding something different beneath.

clue.text: Look at young man going the wrong way, a disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to look at closely

indicators.note: travelling backwards means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A disapproving glance at a youth who has gone off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the young man turns round; SCAN stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a shameful event or state of affairs that causes public outrage, much like a disgrace.

clue.text: Heavenly body's very good when clothed in rough fabric, right?

indicators.note: something dressed in a fabric is wrapped inside it

parts.note: jute is a coarse fibre used for sacking
pi is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Someone with a fine body looks good even dressed in sackcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' as pious, shortened, is a crossword standby; 'Heavenly body' sounds like praise for someone's figure, but it names a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, an astronomical object in the sky.

clue.text: Leather strap, one around a female

parts.note: a jess is a short leather strap fastened to a hawk's leg
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: A falconer's strap looped round a hen bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but it gives CA, the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica is a girl's given name, made popular by Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Cast aside, in two parts as it were

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the actors in a production

definitions.text: aside, in two parts as it were
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split into two words, aside becomes 'a side', a sporting team

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw something away, split into two pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast aside reads as discarding; instead each half defines the answer, and the second needs its letters split as 'a side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Players are both the actors in a theatrical cast and the members who make up a sports team.

clue.text: Business information put into account before start of year

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An office instruction to get the details entered in the ledger before the new year.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a particular service, so a commercial enterprise or organisation.

clue.text: Poison may turn nice day nasty

indicators.note: turning something changes its order, so these letters are rearranged
turned nasty means changed for the worse, reinforcing the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sinister warning that a toxin could ruin a pleasant outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a fast-acting lethal compound, a classic toxin of detective fiction.

clue.text: Drama instructor comes in vintage vehicle

parts.note: the stage stands for theatre or drama
a coach is a trainer or instructor

explanation.surface: A theatre teacher makes an entrance in a classic car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes in' looks like an insertion signal, but nothing goes inside anything; it simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach was a horse-drawn passenger carriage on a regular route, an old form of transport.

clue.text: Till the cows come home here?

definitions.text: Till the cows come home here?

parts.note: surface reading: the idiom for an indefinitely long time

parts.words: Till the cows come home here?
parts.note: setter's reading: a place where you till the soil and where the cows return each evening

explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' is not 'until' but the verb to plough, and the cows really do come home to this place.
explanation.definitionFit: An agricultural holding is where land is cultivated and where livestock such as dairy cattle are housed.

clue.text: Painter turned up two hours before midday

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upwards means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: two hours before noon is ten in the morning

explanation.surface: An artist who arrived at ten in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French artist, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Make fun of artist, character coming last repeatedly

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the letter that comes last in the alphabet, written twice

explanation.surface: Mocking an artist whose character always comes bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: To razz is an informal American word meaning to tease or ridicule someone.

clue.text: Something on the building site to make yours truly smile

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: Something seen among the builders that cheers the speaker up.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-beam is a steel girder with an I-shaped cross-section, used in construction work.

clue.text: One short meal allocation — and what Oliver would have liked!

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A workhouse portion so meagre that Oliver Twist asked for more.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Oliver Twist the boy famously asks for more gruel; a repeat of his helping is what he wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Iteration means repetition, doing something again, and Oliver wanted his serving done once more.

clue.text: Sailors from 'ere getting leave

parts.note: hence means from here; with the h dropped, as the clue's ''ere' does, it becomes 'ence

explanation.surface: A Cockney sailor asking for shore leave to get away from this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ere shows a Cockney dropped H, so the matching word for 'from here' loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave of absence is permitted time away, so leave and absence are synonyms for time off work.

clue.text: Party enjoyment — I being hugged may be most stupid

indicators.note: something hugged is held within arms, so it sits inside another word

explanation.surface: Someone getting hugged at a party, having fun, may come across as rather daft.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozy is informal British for slow-witted, so its superlative describes the dimmest of a group.
